name: Verb Tense Consistency
description: Analyzes the distribution, shifts, and long-range temporal logic of verb tenses throughout a document. Large Language Models struggle with maintaining complex, non-linear timelines. They heavily favor simple tenses (simple present or simple past) and prioritize local grammatical consistency over macroscopic narrative time. Consequently, AI writing often flattens complex temporal relationships, avoiding nuanced tenses like the past perfect ('had been doing') or future progressive ('will be doing'). Furthermore, when LLMs do shift tenses across long passages, the shifts are often jarring and logically unanchored, driven by changes in the immediate prompt context rather than genuine narrative necessity.
algorithm: Temporal Anchor Tracking & Tense Transition Matrix
mechanism: The algorithm extracts all verbs and their associated morphological tenses using Parts-of-Speech (POS) tagging and dependency parsing. It constructs a 'temporal timeline' of the document. The system calculates the ratio of simple tenses to complex/perfect tenses, and evaluates the logic of tense shifts (e.g., shifting from past to present without a valid rhetorical marker). A text exhibiting an unnaturally rigid adherence to a single simple tense, a lack of complex relational tenses, or mathematically arbitrary tense jumping across paragraph boundaries, is strongly indicative of generative AI.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing creative writing, historical essays, case studies, and biographical content where tracing a complex, multi-layered timeline is essential to the narrative.
strengths:
• Targets a fundamental limitation in LLMs: the lack of a true internal 'world model' of time, forcing them to rely purely on surface-level grammatical probabilities.
• Highly resilient to basic paraphrasing, as changing the temporal structure requires a complete rewrite of the narrative.
limitations:
• Less effective on software documentation, scientific abstracts, or instructional guides, which are structurally required to maintain a strict, flat 'simple present' tense by human authors as well.
• May flag non-native human writing that struggles with complex English tense rules.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Morphological Extraction & Timeline Mapping
Metric: Complex-to-Simple Tense Ratio & Invalid Transition Frequency
Output: 0-100 Temporal Artificiality Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 71-85% accuracy. Its effectiveness scales exponentially with document length; longer documents force the LLM to manage a longer timeline, thereby increasing the probability of detectable temporal flattening.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
